title: Uptime governance roadmap and communication protocol (initiative brief)
content:
Purpose:
Short working brief to align Eng, Product, Platform, and Customer Success on a governance-driven rollout for our Reliability Program (SLOs + operational model). This doc focuses on communication channels, decision gates, owner mapping, and a lightweight canary/cutover plan for per-route SLO adoption across hosted API and Dedicated clusters.

Context and problem statement:
- We have many independent SLO pilots across teams; lacking consistent gating and communication causes duplication and surprise oncall load.
- Product owners want predictable latency budgets; infra wants capacity predictability and less churn in autoscaling policies.
- Goal: Create a repeatable, light-touch governance flow that coordinates changes to SLIs/SLOs, dashboards, runbooks, and rollout policies.

Scope (what this covers):
- Definition + approval flow for service SLIs and SLOs (latency, error-rate, availability, tail latency).
- Cross-functional communication protocol for design reviews, canary windows, and production cutovers.
- Minimal artifact checklist for any SLO change (dashboards, runbook, alert tuning, cost impact).
- Escalation matrix and contingency fallback policies (model variant / lower-QPS routing).
- Metrics and experiment tracking for 90-day adoption pilots.

Out of scope:
- Deep instrumentation rewrites (those go to infra backlog), major infra refactors, and billing model changes.

Key principles (guiding decisions):
- Incrementalism: favor staged adoption, start with shadowing for 2 weeks before enforcement.
- Measurable gates: every change needs a pre-defined signal to roll forward/rollback.
- Low ceremony: maintain a 3-step approval flow for non-customer-impacting SLO tweaks; heavier signoff only for SLA-level changes.
- Cross-team visibility: all SLO assets live in the Reliability namespace in Grafana and Confluence, links in the PR.

Stakeholder roles (RACI-lite):
- Requesting PO (R): Product or service owner proposing SLO change; drafts the RFC and cost/quality trade-off.
- SRE Lead (A): Final approver for rollout readiness and operational impact (pager capacity, runbook completeness).
- Observability Owner (C): Confirms dashboards, SLI instrumentation, and alert thresholds are valid.
- Platform/Infra (C): Confirms autoscaling/placement implications and capacity windows.
- Customer Success (I/C): Informed for externally-visible SLO changes or when customers will be impacted.

Decision gates and approval flow (lightweight):
1) RFC draft (PO) + initial signal targets (SLIs, calculation windows, burn rate thresholds) -> post in #reliability-rfc with summary and confluence link.
2) 72-hour async review period. Observability and Platform must add comments or request meeting.
3) SRE Lead greenlight for canary -> schedule canary window and add to reliability calendar.
4) Canary (shadow -> partial enforcement -> full enforcement). Post-canary retrospective and final signoff.

Artifacts checklist before canary (submit as checklist in PR):
- Confluence RFC page: objective, expected user impact, SLI definition, calculation examples
- Grafana dashboard: SLI panels (p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, traffic distribution)
- Runbook stub: symptoms, mitigation steps, rollback instructions, owner contacts
- Cost delta estimate: expected QPS->tokens cost change or capacity shift (infra estimate)
- Testing plan: load test scenario, key tickets, and canary traffic percentage schedule

Canary cadence suggestion (template):
- Day 0-3: Shadowing only (measure divergences between current and proposed SLI calculation).
- Day 4-7: Partial enforcement (5-10% of traffic routed to SLO-enforced path).
- Day 8-14: Progressive ramp to 50% if signals OK.
- Post 14 days: Full enforcement and retrospective.

Safety/fallbacks and automated rollback triggers:
- Immediate rollback if p99 latency delta > 2x baseline for 1 hour or error-rate jump > 0.5%.
- Auto-failover to alternate model variant or lower-QPS routing policy if backend capacity saturated.
- Manual override via SRE Lead for business-critical customer impacts.

Cross-functional communication protocol (channels and cadence):
- RFC posting: #reliability-rfc (summary + confluence link).
- Weekly coordination sync: 30min cadence for active pilots (SRE + Obs + Platform + PO).
- Canary-day Slack channel: ephemeral single channel per canary (naming: canary-<service>-YYYYMMDD) with pinned runbook and oncall rota.
- Post-mortem/retrospective: Confluence page + short summary to #reliability-updates.

Templates (to copy into RFC or PR):
- RFC header: Owner, proposed change, SLIs affected, expected user-visible difference, rollback criteria, test plan, linked dashboards.
- Dashboard template: panels (latency histograms, traffic heatmap, success-rate over time, burn-rate).
- Runbook stub: symptom -> check 3 metrics -> mitigation steps -> contacts.

Dependency map (quick notes):
- Serving runtime: KV cache behavior and prefix caching can change p95 tail; need Obs to validate cache hits.
- Router service: rollout of weighted routing affects canary percentages; infra to provide safe window for config changes.
- Billing/usage: Product finance must review SLO enforcement that may increase token usage.
- Customer-impacting endpoints: CS pre-notification required for SLA boundary shifts.

Risk heatmap (rough):
- High risk: model-variant fallbacks that are untested against real traffic (requires a full test harness).
- Medium risk: SLI calculation changes that alter historical comparisons (need migration strategy).
- Low risk: dashboard aesthetic changes or alert wording updates.

Experiment tracking & metrics for adoption (90-day):
- Primary success metric: fraction of services adopting governance flow with no >1hr unplanned page events during canary.
- Secondary: mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLO violations, mean time to mitigate (MTTM) after canary adoption.
- Track: number of SLO PRs per month, average review time, rollback rate.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes):
- How prescriptive should SLI calculation windows be? (fixed 5m/1h/24h vs. service-specific)
- When to require finance signoff? Only for changes with >5% cost delta?
- Who owns the canonical SLO history when we change calculation? Do we keep both old and new for 90 days?

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- PO: draft RFC for Auth service SLO change (Priya) -> due 2026-06-22
- Observability: add dashboard template and example panels (Ethan) -> due 2026-06-25
- Platform: provide weighted-routing safe-window guide (Diego) -> due 2026-06-28
- SRE Lead: finalize rollback automation playbook (Marina) -> due 2026-07-05

Notes-to-self / working items (low-ceremony):
- Add a small test harness for shadow SLI comparisons (bench script + sample traffic).
- Keep a lightweight decision log (one-line entries) in Confluence - link in RFCs.
- Consider 1x in-person reliability kickoff with Product PMs for the top 10 services.

Appendix: example SLI definitions (short):
- Success-rate SLI: ratio of 2xx/stream-OK responses over 1h windows, rolling 24h burn rate.
- Latency SLI: p95 < 180ms for API route /v1/generate at 512 tokens median workload.
- Availability SLI: 99.95% over 30-day window (applies to public customer-facing routes).

Quick links (placeholders):
- Canonical dashboards -> grafana/reliability/uptime-catalog
- RFC template -> confluence/Reliability-RFC-Template
- Decision log -> confluence/Reliability-Decision-Log

Scratch / unresolved TODOs:
- Confirm naming convention for ephemeral canary channels (Lena)
- Draft a 2-slide exec summary for BU leads once we have pilot metrics

-- end working draft --

(rough style: intentionally pragmatic, checklist-first, with room for team-specific nuance. This doc is meant to be copied into a confluence RFC and used as the basis for the first pilots.)
